title: Tets Alexander, Nashville musicians and Nat Tolles
summary: He names players who worked with him, a student of his banjo, and Nat Tolles of Monroe.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, Tets used to play with us too, Tets, Alexander. He was a wonderful, my sister. And this other boy, they'd come down there working with Sidney, and they stayed there in town, Boots and his brother, you know, used to work in them Jitney's house. Austin and Thorpe. Spoke and his brother. Spoke with the Saxon and Boots was his base pair. Yeah, young. Yeah, young. Well they're not from here, huh? They're from Nashville.

Now Percy's affair, when I lived on Robinson Street, I was working at a food company, well I took with a stroke in my arm. Well I learned him a little bit, I learned on banjo and he come back here with handing them from out of Baton Rouge, he was playing more banjo than I was, you know what I was. And he played with a, last time I read music, he was up there in Bill Platt or somewhere, he's on piano now. Well I heard he was in that just for a while.
I wanted to be looking for him in that just for a while.
Yeah, Bill Platt, that's where he is.

He was playing piano. He was playing with, what's that boy's name, I used to be on the Al C. Page, you ever run across him? No. Out of Monroe, you met Ben Boyden? I heard of him. Yeah, he's dead now. And Nat Tolles, you remember him?

Nat Tolles. Nat Tolles is from here. He used to play with Louis DeMaine. And he went up there and made the Queen and everything. See Monroe, they've got a bridge between it. Desiree's speech, that's DeMaine's speech. They've got East Monroe and West Monroe and he had a band out of Army Hall in Nebraska and got a little Joe, one of his trumpet players, blew his way. He kind of, I don't know, they say he was off, but he's around here somewhere. Now, he played for plenty of trumpet, he don't play with nobody. He ain't got a horn. We used to play with Nat Tolles. Joe Bentley.
We had Nat Tolles lay down on his back and play a piece. Now, you know. Well, I was going to ask you about some more things.
